## Table 1 — Arms

Safety metric first. ARR is trivially maximised by acting recklessly,
so it is never printed above the rate of acting wrongly.

|-----|----:|----:|----:|----:|--------:|--:|
| human | — | — | — | — | — | 0 |
| runbook | 0.5455 | 0.0000 | 0.6452 | 0.0000 | 0.6452 | 31 |
| naive-llm | — | — | — | — | — | 0 |
| pashupatastra | 0.0000 | 0.3548 | 0.6452 | 0.0000 | 0.8387 | 31 |

**Arms with no data, and why:**

- `human` — not run — requires operators. A simulated human is the number this work would most like to see and the one nobody would check
- `naive-llm` — not run — requires a configured model. The deterministic stub would produce a second runbook under an LLM label

## Table 2 — Ablations

Only components the arm actually exercises can be ablated. Removing a
stage that never ran returns the baseline score and would be reported
as *no effect*, which reads as evidence the component does not matter.

| Variant | FRR | HIR | ARR | Correct | n |
|---------|----:|----:|----:|--------:|--:|
| full architecture | 0.0000 | 0.3548 | 0.6452 | 0.8387 | 31 |
| −no-policy | — | — | — | — | 0 |
| −no-verification | — | — | — | — | 0 |

**Ablations that cannot be measured here:**

- `−hypothesis-evidence`, `−smriti`, `−adjacency` — all three sit in the reasoning path, which the benchmark arm never invokes

## Table 4 — Metrics not computed

Defined in METRICS.md and absent from the tables above. Listed so a
reader does not mistake five reported metrics for all of them.

| Metric | Why it is absent |
|--------|------------------|
| RCA@1 / RCA@3 | root-cause accuracy needs the reasoning layer, which the benchmark arm does not invoke — the shared proposer stands in for diagnosis because there is no configured model. Scoring the stub would measure a fixture this repository wrote |
| Detection precision / recall | the harness injects the fault and hands the arm an already-scoped incident, so nothing in the run exercises detection or correlation |
| MTTR | the recorded clock covers provision → inject → decide, not detection → verified resolution. Reporting it against the METRICS.md definition would be a different quantity under the same name |
